newsitem.title: PERU: Chevron says still eying Petroperu selloff.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says still eying Petroperu selloff.

text.p: U.S.-based Chevron Corp continues to be interested in taking part in the privatization of units of Peruvian state oil company Petroperu, a company official said.
"As soon as other Petroperu assets are offered, we will be ready to evaluate our possible participation," Larry Decker, Chevron's exploration manager, told Reuters.

Peru, which plans to sell in a piecemeal fashion all of Petroperu, has already sold off a refinery, two production lots and a lubricants plant. It plans to further spin off more refineries, wells, sales terminals, transport facilities and its North Peruvian oil line.
"We participated in the auction of Petroperu's lubricants plant, but unfortunately we were not successful," Dekker said.
The Petrolube plant was bought last year by Mobil Corp. of the United States for $18.86 million.
Chevron recently completed seismic studies on oil Lot 52 in Peru's southwestern jungle, where it holds a 40-year exploration and development contract.
"Chevron continues to study and evaluate other opportunities to invest in exploration in Peru (but) there is still no definite prospect of this kind," he said.
Dekker said Chevron's lubricants operations in Peru have "in just two years achieved significant shares of all the different types of markets, such as automobiles, mining, fishing and industrial."
